summary: The target-only comparison is not yet a clean counterfactual: 4,819,575 records with unavailable target status are silently treated as non-target, and the table-subtraction analysis never compares the target-only and all-model linkage runs directly. Preserve unknown target status and score the two newly generated link files on identical records before using the results. The merge guards and spread-statistics calculations are otherwise well defended.

findings.title: Millions of records without measured target status are assigned to the non-target arm
findings.what_the_code_does: The code computes `tgt = !(namefrst==namefrst_fs & namelast==namelast_fs)`, saves only `keep if tgt`, and then executes `replace tgt = 0 if _merge==1`. Consequently, a known commercial-source agreement and an ID absent from `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` receive the same value. The committed brief reports 4,819,575 such absent divided-file records.
findings.why_it_matters: Those records have not been shown to be non-targets, yet lines 111-114 force them to use Ancestry names. Their names can affect their own links and other records through candidate competition. The output is therefore target-only within the labeled universe, not necessarily replacement only on true target records across the linkage universe.
findings.how_to_check: Merge a divided file against a full ID list from `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` carrying an `observed=1` marker, then run `count if _merge==1`, `count if _merge==1 & age>=10 & age<.`, and tabulate birthplace. Repeat over all files or use `tgt_fallback_diag.do`; then compare links involving these IDs and age-nearby candidate sets under Ancestry versus model-name treatment.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain a three-way status: observed target, observed non-target, and unavailable. Recover the commercial comparison for unavailable records where possible; otherwise exclude them symmetrically or report sensitivity runs assigning them first to Ancestry and then to model names. Label the resulting estimand accordingly.

findings.title: The non-target subtraction does not compare all-record replacement with target-only replacement
findings.what_the_code_does: The script subtracts each target-table count from the corresponding full-table count and compares the global Old and New linkage runs. It never reads `link1930_1940_mltgt1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta`. Moreover, ABE runs `abematch ... unique_m(2) unique_f(2)` and defines retained uniqueness using `unique_file2 == 1 & unique_match2 == 1`, so changing target names can alter non-target outcomes through candidate competition.
findings.why_it_matters: The reported non-target decline cannot isolate the effect of replacing names on non-target records: both target and non-target names change between Old and New. Using it to choose between all-record and target-only replacement could support the wrong implementation.
findings.how_to_check: Score `link1930_1940_mltgt1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` and `link1930_1940_ml1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` on the identical observed non-target IDs. Merge their pairs by census ID and tabulate retained links, changed partners, and Verified/Unverifiable/Contradicted classifications.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the target-only and all-model linkage outputs for the policy comparison. Keep the All-minus-Target results only as a descriptive decomposition of the existing global Old-versus-New runs, explicitly noting that they do not identify the marginal effect of replacing non-target names.

findings.title: Permitted fallback discrepancies can make the two linkage runs differ without any model-name substitution
findings.what_the_code_does: The builder counts `name_true_cleaned_exists==0 & !(f_name==f_ans & l_name==l_ans)` but now exits only when `nbad > 0.001*nchk`, allowing the documented 436 discrepancies. For any such non-target record, lines 111-114 put `_ans_cleaned` into the target-only input while the all-record input retains the differing `_true_cleaned` fallback, despite neither version using a model transcription.
findings.why_it_matters: If any discrepancies are non-targets, the runs differ for an unintended cleaning-path reason that can alter links and candidate uniqueness. The affected share is small, but the global tolerance does not establish that its link-level effect is zero.
findings.how_to_check: Before replacement, accumulate `count if name_true_cleaned_exists==0 & !(f_name==f_ans & l_name==l_ans) & !tgt`. After both link files exist, identify changed assignments involving those IDs or their competing candidates.
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile the fallback-cleaning paths or require zero discrepancies specifically among non-target records. If temporarily retained, report the consequential count and demonstrate that excluding affected candidates leaves the comparison unchanged.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so manuscript claims could not be checked; claims-vs-code review was limited to code comments and committed review briefs.
The external census and divided-file datasets were unavailable, so the documented 4,819,575 unknown-status records and 436 fallback discrepancies could not be independently reproduced or classified.
The Stata pipeline and user-written matching commands were not run; runtime consequences are inferred from source semantics and committed run summaries.
The four external TeX inputs to `nontarget_from_tables.py` were readable and the Python script ran successfully, but their upstream generation was not rerun.
`MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw_sd.md` was not present, so the new spread table's numerical output could not be inspected.
This was a review of commit range `e3ca71f^..7fbb923` plus necessary surrounding code, not a full-repository audit.
